collectible:2.text: The city of Riften has two people capable of handling this task: Maul, an associate of Maven Black-Briar, and Vex, a member of the Thieves Guild. After the appraisal, it is revealed that a total of 24 Stones of Barenziah exist, which activates the quest "No Stone Unturned." The stones are quest items of 0.5 weight and worth 200 , and they cannot be removed from the inventory until the entire set is obtained.

easter-egg:1.text: When the Dragonborn completes No One Escapes Cidhna Mine in the favor of Thonar Silver-Blood, he apologizes and gives the Dragonborn his family ring, saying that the Silver-Bloods pay their debts. This may be a reference to the unofficial motto of the Lannister house, "A Lannister always pays his debts."

easter-egg:2.text: At night along roads you have a chance of encountering a spectral horseman without a head galloping along at full tilt. He carries an axe on his back, which is likely a reference to Washington Irving's The Legend of Sleepy Hollow. If you follow him, he eventually takes you to Hamvir's Rest, where there are several skeletons, and a leveled draugr to fight and a Master chest.

easter-egg:3.text: If he is a follower and you enter a cave, Belrand will say, "When I was a boy, my friends and I used to play 'seek the wumpus' in caves much like this," a reference to the classic video game Hunt the Wumpus.

easter-egg:4.text: In Whiterun, the giant tree there is called the Gildergreen. It is grown from the Eldergleam, the oldest living thing in Skyrim, but it is dying. This is similar to the Gondorian capital of Minas Tirith in Lord of the Rings: Return of the King, where the legendary White Tree faces a similar fate.

easter-egg:5.text: The city of Whiterun greatly resembles Edoras, the capital of Rohan; both cities are built atop a bluff, with the palace at the top of the hill and have a horse portrayed on their banner.

easter-egg:6.text: During "A Night to Remember," one of the tasks is to obtain a wedding ring from a Hagraven named Moira, who will say, "My precious" while trying to get the ring from her, referencing Gollum.

easter-egg:7.text: Faerengar Secret-Fire's name is a direct reference to Gandalf's declaration in Moria, "I am a servant of the Secret Fire."

easter-egg:8.text: The Notched Pickaxe is a reference to "Notch," the creator of Minecraft. As a pickaxe, it is used for mining and it also has an enchantment that boosts Smithing, Skyrim's method of crafting. It is located just below the very top of The Throat of the World. Climb your way up the remaining part of the mountain by jumping and you should arrive there.

easter-egg:9.text: In Endon's House in Markarth, look for a shelf in the back of the room with Sliced Goat Cheese, a row of Garlic, and some Glow Dust arranged to look like a scene from Pac-Man.

easter-egg:10.text: In Skuldafn, one of the fireplaces contains a potato, a boiled creme treat, and three pieces of charcoal placed in such a way that it resembles Portal 2's character GLaDOS in her potato battery form.

easter-egg:11.text: A generic piece of dialogue sometimes uttered by male drunks and bandits during a brawl is "Remember... hit the one in the middle!" This is the advice given by Paulie in Rocky IV to help Rocky overcome double vision, which can be caused by both drunkenness and head trauma.

easter-egg:12.text: Inside Blackreach, you will find a building called the War Quarters. Inside these quarters, one will find one room with seven small beds placed in a circle around a lantern. This may be a reference to Snow White and the Seven Dwarves. Opposite of the bedroom is a hallway and at the end another bedroom, where a much larger double-bed is found.

easter-egg:13.text: In the village of Ivarstead, there is a woman named Temba Wide-Arm. This is a reference to the Star Trek: The Next Generation episode Darmok, where one of the often-repeated phrases is "Temba, his arms wide."

easter-egg:14.text: Inside of Bleakcoast Cave (Eastern Winterhold), there is a skeleton hanging upside down from the ceiling. Below the skeleton is a glowing greatsword. This is a reference to Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back when Luke Skywalker was caught on Hoth and hung from the cavern ceiling. The sword below represents his lightsaber.

easter-egg:15.text: On your way to Hag Rock Redoubt, there is a bridge with a dead Troll underneath. If it is your first time visiting, you will witness two goats meeting a third at the end of the bridge then running off together. This is a reference to the fairy tale, Three Billy Goats Gruff, where a troll is defeated by a trio of goats. A similar reference was made in Oblivion.

easter-egg:16.text: Upon entering the first hall of Swindler's Den, there is a practice dummy with a red apple perched atop its head. This is a reference to the Swiss story of William Tell, who had to shoot an apple off of his son's head.

easter-egg:17.text: M'aiq reappears in . He appeared in and, as an Easter Egg Basket of sorts for developers to comment on some of the game features that were removed, added, or were/are planned for the series as well as other RPG gaming community related remarks.

easter-egg:18.text: The Sweetroll can be found throughout Skyrim as a normal food item, and is sometimes placed in strange locations.

easter-egg:19.text: At times, a hold guard will remark "Let me guess, someone stole your sweetroll."
